summary.text: 友 combines two hand forms, 又, traditionally associated with friendship. The character means “friend” or “companion”; the hands’ precise contribution and whether they also cue the sound remain debated.

formation.text: 友 is a disputed semantic or phono-semantic compound. The two 又 forms are identified as hands and linked with friendship; one account also assigns 又 a phonetic role. The evidence does not determine whether one or both forms provide that sound cue.

components.text: 又 depicts a hand. In 友, two such forms are described as facing the same way and sometimes joined, supporting a two-hands interpretation. Some accounts treat them as semantic; another also gives 又 a phonetic role, but its placement is unresolved.

sound_limitation.text: Old Chinese comparisons make a phonetic contribution plausible but do not identify whether one or both repeated 又 forms provide it. The modern Mandarin resemblance alone does not establish an ancient sound role.

sound.text: The Mandarin readings are similar, but that modern resemblance alone does not establish an ancient sound relationship.
The Middle Chinese reconstructions are similar, with different tone categories.
In this reconstruction, the forms share initial and most rhyme material but differ in the final element, making a phonetic connection plausible without proving the component’s role.
The forms likewise share initial and medial/rime material but differ in the final element.

history.text: Oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, and small-seal forms are reported. Early forms are described as two similarly oriented hands, sometimes joined; in small seal the forms are arranged vertically. This records changes in layout, without establishing a particular scene of cooperation.
The received Shuowen explanation connects the two 又 forms with people who share aims and interact as friends. This is a traditional interpretation of the graph.

uncertainties.text: Accounts differ on whether the two 又 forms contribute meaning alone or also sound. Sound comparisons support a possible phonetic role but do not determine which repeated form has which function.

The earliest reported contexts include a personal name and a sacrificial use read as 侑. The evidence does not establish “friend” as the earliest attested sense or a continuous path from those early uses to later friend and associate uses.
A Mawangdui manuscript is reported to use 友 to write 柔, “soft.” This is a separate use of the whole graph for another word; the supplied account does not establish the sound basis for the borrowing.

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, 漢字構形資料庫
evidence.text: Lists oracle-bone forms (two examples), bronze forms (including inscription 集成04178), Chu manuscripts, and small seal. Its account says the bronze/oracle form depicts two 又 (hands) oriented alike, even joined, to indicate friendliness; in small seal, the two 又 shapes were arranged vertically. This supports a semantic “two hands” analysis but does not establish that the depicted cooperation was the historically intended concept.
evidence.title: 漢字「友」：字形演變

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 形義通解; 甲骨、金文用例
evidence.text: Presents both a semantic and phonetic account: the two 同向又 shapes suggest friendliness, and 又 also serves as phonetic. It reports oracle-bone use for a personal name and a reading as 侑 in a sacrificial context; bronze inscriptions use 友 for friend/friendly or associates, citing 趞曹鼎「用卿(饗)朋友」, 牆盤「隹(惟)辟孝友」, and 令方彝「乃寮與乃友」. It also records a loan reading 柔 in the Mawangdui Laozi manuscripts, with甲本「友弱勝強」 corresponding to乙本「柔弱勝強」. The page does not provide absolute dates for these individual witnesses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：友

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: Reports the received Shuowen account: 「同志為友。从二又。相交友也」, glossing 友 as those sharing purposes and describing the graph as two 又. Its definitions and examples include a noun ‘friend’, the verb ‘make friends/be acquainted’ with a Lunyu example, ‘love’, and ‘assist/cooperate’; these are dictionary-organized senses and do not by themselves prove their chronological order.
evidence.title: A00470 友 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Dong Chinese
evidence.text: Identifies two 又 components, each glossed as hand and as contributing sound, and gives the character’s reported Old Chinese *[ɢ]ʷəʔ, Middle Chinese hjuwX, and Mandarin yǒu. context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The graph's earliest contexts available here are reported as Shang oracle-bone personal-name and 侑 sacrificial uses; these do not establish ‘friend’ as its earliest attested sense. Individual oracle-bone and bronze witnesses were not independently inspected as primary artifacts, and the dictionary page provides no absolute dates for the cited inscriptions.

The semantic ‘two cooperating hands’ account and the phono-semantic account are not mutually exclusive in all sources: CUHK explicitly gives 又 both semantic and phonetic roles. The exact contribution of each repeated 又 shape remains unresolved; no independent phonetic comparison in the same reconstruction system was verified for 友 and 又 beyond reported Zhengzhang values.

No sound-loan claim for the entire graph 友 is required by the evidence examined. The Mawangdui 友-for-柔 spelling is reported by CUHK, but its underlying reading is a separate lexical loan, not an explanation of graph formation.

The stated semantic extension chain from personal name/侑 to friend, verb ‘befriend’, and ‘friendly’ is not established. The sources attest distinct contextual uses; a continuous chronology or semantic bridge should not be asserted.

Official Unicode Unihan records for U+53CB and U+53C8 were attempted but inaccessible through the web tool. The supplied local kMandarin row supports yǒu for 友; no local row was supplied for 又. An official Unicode click-through citation could not be verified.
No licensed-bulk-reuse terms were verified for the recurring character database material; cite character-specific pages rather than recommending a local extract.

The separate historical dictionarial evidence supplies Zhengzhang and Baxter–Sagart reconstructions in the dossier, but this run externally verified neither pair directly; the local Baxter–Sagart rows were checked as provided and retain that system's notation. The role of one versus both 又 components remains unresolved.

Earliest reported oracle-bone uses are personal-name and 侑 sacrificial contexts; the available sources do not establish that ‘friend’ is the earliest attested sense. The cited witnesses were not independently inspected as primary artifact records, and absolute dates for each example are not provided.
The stepwise semantic relationship from name or sacrificial 侑 to friend, friendly, associate, or verbal uses is unestablished. Do not derive chronology from the dictionary's sense list.

The Mawangdui 友-for-柔 example is a reported whole-graph loan in a manuscript context, separate from the phonetic role of 又 within the compound graph. No independent phonetic history for the loan pair was verified here.
Unicode Unihan endpoints for U+53CB and U+53C8 were inaccessible, so official click-through records could not be cited despite supplied local kMandarin rows.

The two Commons vector pages were discovered, but file-specific license terms were not verified in accessible page content. No image is selected because the reuse provenance requirement is unmet. No exact Xiaoxuetang character-form record/image URL was retrieved. The character-specific chardb page states All Rights Reserved; it is evidence only. No bulk-reuse terms were verified for repeated dictionary text.

limitations.text: The reported early graph of 友 consists of two 又 shapes, but the available image candidates are modern redraws whose reuse rights are unverified. No usable image is available to show those early forms directly; the two-hands account is reported in the character histories, while the precise contribution of each 又 remains uncertain.
